title: optimize-rotary-qkv-interleave-and-flashv4-block-fusion
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improved attention throughput for long-context serving: new FlashAttention-v4 block fusion and rotary QKV interleaving reduce p99 token latency on GPU instances and lower token cost by up to 18% for chat workloads.
description: Motivation: reduce per-token overhead for long-sequence serving workloads and simplify fallback compatibility across attention variants. Summary: introduces an experimental FlashAttention-v4 block-fusion kernel plus a runtime transform that interleaves rotary-multiplied Q/K/V memory layout to reduce memory touches and improve vectorized loads; adds scheduler hints for continuous-batching to prefer low-latency batches for short requests and high-throughput packing for long requests. Changes include CUDA kernels, C++ runtime wiring, Python integration test updates, and perf harness additions. Design notes: the block-fusion kernel fuses QK compute, rotary application, and softmax scaling into a single fused path for blocks up to 128 tokens, falling back to the existing vectorized path for larger blocks; the QKV interleave transform reorders per-layer KV cache layout to an interleaved Q-K-V contiguous format which improves coalesced global loads on Ampere and Hopper architectures. Backwards compatibility: runtime supports a feature flag (attn.flashv4.enabled) and falls back to previous FlashAttention implementation when models are pinned or the kernel fails safety checks. Rollout plan: gate behind 10% canary on Dedicated, validate with the perf canary job, expand to 50% after 48h if error budget holds, then gradually enable by default. Checklist: [x] unit tests for kernel shaders; [x] integration tests for KV restore across warm restarts; [x] perf harness and baseline numbers added; [x] feature flag and metrics; [x] docs note in perf-tuning.md. Benchmarks (internal, p95/p99 token latency on g4dn equivalent): baseline FlashA-v3: p95=12.8ms, p99=25.3ms; this PR FlashA-v4 w/ interleave: p95=10.4ms (18.7% improvement), p99=20.9ms (17.4% improvement). Cost impact: synthetic request mix shows ~12-18% reduction in token GPU time. Risks and mitigations: fused kernel increases complexity and may surface numerical differences; added deterministic numeric tolerance checks and golden-output evals on a set of regression prompts. Related work: follows up on ENG-2972 (batching scheduler tweaks) and ENG-2150 (kv cache layout experiments).
